headline: Congress cancels a Department of Energy rule that set stricter energy efficiency standards for gas-fired tankless water heaters used in homes.
what_it_does: This law uses the Congressional Review Act to cancel a Department of Energy rule submitted on December 26, 2024. That rule would have raised the energy efficiency standards for consumer gas-fired instantaneous (tankless) water heaters. With the rule cancelled, the stricter standards do not take effect. Under the Congressional Review Act, the agency generally cannot issue a substantially similar rule unless Congress later authorizes it.

who_it_affects.group: Companies that make gas-fired tankless water heaters
who_it_affects.how: They will not have to meet the stricter efficiency standards the rule would have required.

who_it_affects.group: Homeowners and renters who buy gas-fired tankless water heaters
who_it_affects.how: The models available to them will not have to meet the higher efficiency levels the rule set.
The agency's rule is cancelled, and it is generally barred from issuing a substantially similar rule without new approval from Congress.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted May 9, 2025; the rule is treated as having no force or effect.
